Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back. The players and umpires return to the park. Suzie Bates and Georgia Plimmer are the openers for the New Zealand Women. It will be Sugandika Kumari with the ball for Sri Lanka Women. Here we go!
…THE RUN CHASE…

Right then, New Zealand Women need 116 in 20 overs to keep their chances alive and kicking in the competition. They will have to bat well as Sri Lanka Women have good bowlers in their ranks. Can they do it or will Sri Lanka Women get their first win of the tournament? We shall find out. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

Leigh Kasperek is up for a chat. She says that it was pretty warm. Adds that they got off to a solid start but are glad about how they pulled things back. Mentions that she knew it was going to be hot but lauds the girls on the sidelines who keep them cool in these conditions. Shares that the pitch is good and it is coming out nicely, but adds that it is a little bit sticky and they can chase it down.

For New Zealand Women, Leigh Kasperek and Melie Kerr were the pick of the bowlers with two wickets each while Eden Carson got the solitary wicket of Vishmi Gunarathne. They bowled and fielded according to plans but managed only the solitary wicket in the first ten overs. The White Ferns did well in the second half to take a few quick wickets in a heap which restricted the run scoring for Sri Lanka Women.

A much better batting effort from Sri Lanka Women helps them post their highest score of the tournament. Batting first, Sri Lanka Women lost Vishmi Gunarathne early but Chamari Athapaththu and Harshitha Samarawickrama batted well and 48 for the second wicket. The dismissal of Chamari Athapaththu brought a mini slide as the Asian side were reduced to 97 for 5. Nilakshika Silva and Ama Kanchana made handy runs in the lower order and finished with a competitive total.
A couple to end the innings! Floated, full, on the middle and leg. Ama Kanchana skips down and lofts it toward long-on for a two more. Sri Lanka Women end with a fighting score of 115 for 5.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with pre-match formalities and we are set for the action to begin. Chamari Athapaththu and Vishmi Gunarathne stride out to open the batting for Sri Lanka Women. It will be Rosemary Mair with the ball for New Zealand Women. Let's play...

All in readiness now as the teams and match officials make their way to the ground for the National Anthems. We start with the anthem of Sri Lanka Women, followed by that of New Zealand Women. Live action is not far away.

PITCH REPORT - Ian Bishop is near the pitchside alongside Anjum Chopra. They share that there is glorious sunshine with the temperature being 38 degrees and the players will be tested. Bishop further adds that the boundaries are 57m and 62m square down the ground it will be 73m. Anjum Chopra adds that the teams are going with more spin options and the batters will look to play late and allow the ball to come on.

Sophie Devine, the New Zealand Women, says that they were looking to bat first as well. Shares that Leigh Kasperek comes in for Fran Jonas. Mentions that they need to keep Sri Lanka Women under 120 and try to chase as well as they can. Adds that they have not thought about NRR and they are focussing on a game at a time with results taking care of themselves.

Chamari Athapaththu has won the toss and opted to BAT first. She says that the batting hasn’t gone to plan but they will back the batters. Adds that things have not gone their way but the belief is there in the camp and they are looking to play with positive mindset. Ends by sharing that Sachini Nisansala comes in for Inoka Ranaweera.

Sri Lanka Women (Playing XI) - Vishmi Gunarathne, Chamari Athapaththu(C), Harshitha Samarawickrama, Kaveesha Dilhari, Nilakshika Silva, Inoshi Fernando, Ama Kanchana, Anushka Sanjeewani(WK), Sugandika Kumari, Sachini Nisansala (in place of Inoka Ranaweera), Udeshika Prabodani.

New Zealand Women (Playing XI) - Suzie Bates, Georgia Plimmer, Melie Kerr, Sophie Devine(C), Brooke Halliday, Maddy Green, Izzy Gaze(WK), Leigh Kasperek (in place of Fran Jonas), Rosemary Mair, Lea Tahuhu, Eden Carson.
TOSS UPDATE – Sri Lanka Women have won the toss and opted to BAT.

In contrast, New Zealand Women got their campaign off to a winning start against the India Women but lost by a massive margin against the Australia Women which dented their NRR. Facing the Australian Women, the New Zealand Women bowlers kept them to a modest score of 148 with Melie Kerr, Rosemary Mair, and Brooke Halliday among the wickets. The batting failed to turn up and the White Ferns by dismissed for just 88, losing by 60 runs. With games against Sri Lanka Women and Pakistan Women coming up, the New Zealand Women will be confident to seal the semi-final spot. Can Sri Lanka Women get their first win of the tournament or New Zealand Women prove to be strong for them? Let's find out. Toss and team news coming up shortly.

Hello and welcome to our coverage of Match 15 in the ICC Women’s T20 World Cup, 2024. It’s a Group A clash where Sri Lanka Women will face off against the New Zealand Women at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium in Sharjah. The Asian champions were thrashed by India Women by 82 runs and ended their chances of going further. Sri Lankan bowlers gave away over 170 runs and their batting continued to be dismal as they were bundled out for just 90 runs. Their batting trio of Chamari Athapaththu, Vishmi Gunarathne, and Harshitha Samarawickrama have failed to fire and has affected them badly. Sri Lanka Women are already eliminated from the tournament after three straight losses and will want to the competition on a high with a consolation win.

New Zealand Women and Sri Lanka Women are set to face off in match 15 of the ongoing Women’s T20 World Cup 2024 at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium. The stakes are high for the Sophie Devine-led New Zealand side, as they seek a much-needed victory to keep their hopes alive for the knockout stage. After a strong start by defeating India in their opener, the White Ferns stumbled against defending champions Australia, suffering a heavy defeat that left them with a negative Net Run Rate (NRR) of 0.050. With their qualification for the semi-finals hanging in the balance, New Zealand not only needs to secure a win but must also improve their NRR to strengthen their position. For Sri Lanka, it has been a disappointing tournament. They have lost all three of their matches and are currently sitting at the bottom of the Group A table. The Sri Lankan side, led by Chamari Athapaththu, faced defeats to Pakistan by 31 runs, Australia by six wickets, and India by a staggering 82 runs. As a result, their hopes of making the semi-finals have already been dashed, and the upcoming game will be their last outing in this edition of the tournament. Although the match holds no significance in terms of qualification, Sri Lanka will be aiming to end their campaign on a high note with a consolation victory. New Zealand, on the other hand, will be looking to bounce back from their recent loss and regain the momentum they showcased in their opening match against India. Captain Sophie Devine will play a crucial role in leading her side’s charge, while star players like Suzie Bates, Georgia Plimmer, and Amelia Kerr will need to step up with both bat and ball. New Zealand’s batting lineup has the firepower to post big scores, but they will need to avoid the middle-order collapses that have cost them in previous matches. Their bowling attack, led by Lea Tahuhu and Eden Carson, has shown promise but will need to be sharp to contain the Sri Lankan batters. For Sri Lanka, the tournament has been a tough journey. Their struggles with both bat and ball have been evident, with key players failing to deliver in crucial moments.
